channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [Politico Europe] A huit mois de la présidentielle, les comptes de campagne déjà sous surveillance
item.description: POLITICO a rencontré Christian Charpy, le président de l’autorité administrative qui aura la responsabilité de valider ou non les dépenses des candidats à l’Elysée.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU’s Ribera joins push for first woman to lead UN
item.description: Four women feature among the seven candidates seeking to replace António Guterres when he steps down at the end of the year.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Burnham set to join King Charles at high-stakes Commonwealth summit
item.description: November's Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting will be fraught with jeopardy over calls for slavery reparations.

item.title: [Financial Times] McDonald’s bets on chicken to win back diners as beef prices soar
item.description: Fast-food chain aims to grow share in booming chicken market in bid to kick-start sluggish US sales

item.title: [Politico Europe] German police official Jürgen Ebner selected to lead Europol
item.description: The agency insider will now face European Parliament lawmakers before the Council formally appoints him.

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump’s diesel ban would hurt America and help China
item.description: Suspending foreign sales of the vital fuel may look good in the short term but the US would soon suffer

item.title: [Financial Times] US Treasury yields soar after strong data fuels bets on further rate rises
item.description: Closely followed survey underscores worries parts of the world’s biggest economy are overheating

item.title: [Politico Europe] Qui réussira à financer sa campagne présidentielle ?
item.description: Prêts, appels aux dons, levées de fonds : les équipes des candidats à la présidentielle s’activent pour trouver les moyens de financer leurs campagnes. Qui s’en sort bien ? Qui est à la peine ? Marine Le Pen peut-elle cette année décrocher un prêt auprès d’une banque française alors que l’initiative de Matignon pour offrir […]

item.title: [Financial Times] European diesel prices climb over prospect of US export ban
item.description: Any move by Washington to suspend foreign sales would be ‘catastrophic’ for global supplies, analysts warn

item.title: [DW] Slovakia: PM Robert Fico's NATO Article 5 remarks spark criticism and raise questions about his country's NATO commitment
item.description: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico says he fears war and will do everything he can to keep his country out of one. Critics say his remarks risk weakening NATO, the alliance that was designed to prevent such a war.

item.title: [EU Observer] No Israeli bonds on sale in EU for now, in de facto €2.2bn sanction
item.description: Neither Ireland nor Luxembourg have been authorising sales of Israeli bonds since the start of September, potentially costing Israel €2.2bn a year, as shock over Gaza and West Bank grows.

item.title: [Financial Times] Iran’s president says Tehran ready for talks but hits back at Trump’s ‘bullying’
item.description: US delegation walks out as Masoud Pezeshkian delivers speech

item.title: [Financial Times] What to do when your Waymo holds up a Secret Service motorcade
item.description: Stranded in six-lane traffic, surrounded by agents, my autonomous vehicle refused to budge

item.title: [EU Observer] A Russian tank survived 40 drone strikes, suggesting mechanised warfare could make a comeback (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,672)
item.description: New videos and expert accounts reveal how Russia’s upgraded “tsar tent” tanks, Arena-M defences, and drone-hunting tactics are being tested in real combat long before Moscow admits what is really working.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Vater, Mutter, Kinder – Alice Weidel und das Familienbild der AfD
item.description: Alice Weidel lebt in einer gleichgeschlechtlichen Partnerschaft mit Kindern – ein scharfer Kontrast zum traditionellen Familienbild der AfD. Wie reagiert die Parteichefin, wenn Spitzenkandidaten wie Ulrich Siegmund ihr Lebensmodell öffentlich abwerten und Parteikollegen gegen sexuelle Minderheiten hetzen? Pauline von Pezold und Frederik Schindler analysieren einen internen Kulturkampf, in dem Weidel zunehmend ins Visier der eigenen […]

item.title: [Financial Times] Countries cancel Iran flights after US threatens to ‘shut down’ airlines
item.description: Iraq, Oman and Azerbaijan join growing list of nations suspending air travel after Scott Bessent warns of further sanctions

item.title: [Financial Times] Chinese carmaker unveils sub-5 minute EV battery charging
item.description: Volvo Cars and Lotus owner is among Chinese carmakers seeking to reduce dependence on market leader CATL

item.title: [Politico Europe] Canada seeks deforestation law carveouts as EU ties deepen
item.description: Ottawa complained of "burdensome requirements" for Canadian firms under anti-deforestation rules.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU Commission seeks to release Hungary’s frozen funds
item.description: Péter Magyar has made freeing up the money a key priority since replacing Viktor Orbán as Hungary’s PM after a seismic election victory in May.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Middle powers can’t be bystanders as the UN falters
item.description: Finland and Australia are seeking Security Council seats with a message: The rules-based order needs countries willing to fight for it.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU moves to unlock €4.2bn for Hungary as Magyar strengthens rule-of-law and corruption rules
item.description: The EU Commission proposes to unfreeze billions of euros for Hungary, as changes in the few months since the April election of Peter Magyar become visible.

item.title: [Financial Times] The west does not have a leadership problem
item.description: If Friedrich Merz and almost everyone else is unpopular, perhaps governments aren’t the issue

item.title: [Politico Europe] Germany wants PAC-3 missile production in Europe, Pistorius says
item.description: There is a global shortage of the interceptor missiles, so Germany is hoping for its own production line.

item.title: [EU Observer] Tax the rich, cap the rents: the policy mix helping Europe’s left push back the far-right
item.description: In the last two weeks, leftwing parties have surged across Europe. It is no surprise that leftwing parties running on affordability and wealth redistribution platforms have been gaining ground.

item.title: [DW] Famine threatens the Ukrainian town of Oleshky in the southern Kherson region as Russia delays creating a humanitarian evacuation corridor
item.description: Food supplies to the town of Oleshky in the occupied part of the southern Kherson region have been cut off since May. Efforts by Kyiv to negotiate the evacuation of civilians with Moscow have been largely unsuccessful.

item.title: [EU Observer] Unions rally against new ‘EU Inc’ race-to-bottom on labour laws and pay
item.description: 'EU Inc', or the 28th regime, started as an EU project to facilitate the expansion of small companies. Now, trade unions warn it could erode years of hard-earned labour rights.

item.title: [EU Observer] Montenegro is the question von der Leyen left unanswered
item.description: Europe does not win by inventing fancy titles for its friendships, or by naming the rivals it means to keep out. It wins by being the place its neighbours both choose and can integrate into.

item.title: [Financial Times] UK data centre group left biggest customer ByteDance unnamed in $35bn IPO push
item.description: Chinese tech giant was AI cloud provider’s largest customer last year but is not prominently named in pitch to stock market investors

item.title: [DW] UK: Village votes to 'secede' in asylum center plan protest
item.description: Residents of Piddington, a tiny, remote village in Oxfordshire in England, have staged a "referendum" on leaving the UK. They are objecting to plans to open an asylum reception center at a disused military base nearby.

item.title: [DW] Can Canada and the EU deepen ties to counter Trump?
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is known for standing up to US President Donald Trump. Now he wants to forge a "unique alliance" with Europe. But what could such a partnership look like?

item.title: [DW] Shock in Kosovo as Hague convicts former President Thaci
item.description: The conviction in The Hague of former President Hashim Thaci and three former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has caused consternation in Kosovo — both among political leaders and on the streets. DW reports from Pristina.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Bullies cannot be appeased’: Pressure mounts on EU to shield ICC from new US sanctions
item.description: When the big brother becomes a bully, who stands up to him? The question is no longer simply whether Brussels supports international justice, but whether it is ready to take practical steps to protect it.

item.title: [EU Observer] France bullies EU into delisting top Russian oligarch, angering allies in last-minute showdown
item.description: Ambassadors held three meetings on Monday and two more on Tuesday, as the clock ticked toward the legal collapse of Russia sanctions due to a French veto.

item.title: [EU Observer] Dutch fossil-fuel exit plan shows EU struggle to set binding deadlines
item.description: The Dutch fossil fuel phase-out plan falls short of outlining clear deadlines, as EU countries struggle to fulfil the 2050 climate neutrality goal.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukraine shows how it shoots down jet-powered Russian drones, as Moscow seeks to expand production (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,671)
item.description: Ukraine has finally found ways to hunt Russia’s fastest drones in mid-air, as new satellite images and documents suggest the Kremlin is preparing to flood the battlefield with tens of thousands more.

item.title: [EU Observer] Fourth Russia-linked LNG carrier puts Danish shipyard in new ‘sanctions gamble’
item.description: The Danish yard is repairing one of its own Nato warships while continuing to service LNG carriers from Russia reportedly linked to Russia’s FSB security service.

item.title: [DW] Military aircraft crashes near US air base in Spangdahlem, Germany
item.description: The F-16 pilot was able to safely eject from the plane and was taken to receive medical care. The incident occurred near Spangdahlem Air Base in the German state of Rhineland-Palatinate.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU-Philippines free-trade pact joins Brussels’ growing ‘harvest’ of Asia deals
item.description: An EU-Philippines pact is the latest trade deal to be 'harvested', and Thailand and Malaysia are likely to be next.

item.title: [EU Observer] German minister slams Costa over EU budget, says he has ‘completely lost touch with reality’
item.description: Time is running out for member states to move closer together on the next seven-year budget, with EU leaders aiming to strike a deal by the end of the year. But efforts by European Council president António Costa to bring capitals together in recent weeks have so far yielded little result.

item.title: [EU Observer] What JK Rowling’s Voldemort can teach us about Ukraine war
item.description: Since the start of the Russian full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, as the West decided to support Ukraine in its defensive efforts, Moscow has been sounding exactly like Lord Voldemort: “Give me Ukraine. It cannot win."

item.title: [DW] 'Swan Song': New book by Princess Diana's brother drops
item.description: A memoir penned by Charles Spencer on his older sister's life has been released, opening old royal wounds nearly three decades after Princess Diana's death.

item.title: [EU Observer] The secretive Saudi arms deal with Greece making Athens a democratic ‘black box’
item.description: When a European government enters a military agreement with a foreign power, citizens should not have to wait for a payment dispute or a renewal crisis to discover what their government has agreed to. Greece's Patriot deployment in Saudi Arabia raises precisely this question.

item.title: [DW] Russian birth tourism to Brazil increases
item.description: Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and stricter regulations in Argentina, more and more Russians are choosing to travel to Brazil to give birth to children, who will obtain Brazilian nationality.

item.title: [DW] A war-fatigued and anxious Russia picks a new parliament
item.description: Fuel shortages, drone strikes and mobilization rumors are fueling anxiety and war fatigue in Russia. As support for peace talks grows among Russians, the Kremlin is watching closely ahead of parliamentary elections.

item.title: [DW] Serbian President Vucic criticizes Kosovo war crimes verdict
item.description: The conviction of four former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has drawn sharply different reactions across the Balkans. Serbia has accused the court of failing to fully address crimes against Serbs.

item.title: [DW] King Charles, Earl Spencer clash over Diana death once again
item.description: Buckingham Palace has rejected criticism of King Charles III in a new book by the brother of his late wife, Princess Diana. Earl Charles Spencer has been a fierce critic of his former brother-in-law for decades.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine steps up measures to protect railways
item.description: As Russia increases its attacks on Ukraine's rail infrastructure, the Ukrainian government has called for help to replace destroyed locomotives and is making plans to keep passengers safe.

item.title: [DW] Ever more Israelis moving to and investing in Cyprus
item.description: Over the past three years, more and more Israelis have been purchasing property and investing in Cyprus, with many moving to the island permanently. How has this changed the Cypriot economy and how are locals responding?

item.title: [DW] Airport malaria in Germany remains infrequent
item.description: An outbreak of malaria at Frankfurt Airport this summer has raised alarm. Experts believe parasites probably arrived in a passenger's luggage. But with the onset of fall, the risks of contracting the disease are low.

item.title: [DW] Canada and EU: A look at the bloc's special relationships
item.description: Though Canada may be some distance from Europe geographically, closer political ties are in the cards. With talk of an associate membership, DW takes a look at other arrangements the EU has with particular countries.
